# Embassy v1.9.0 — Embassy is a network

Your machines already trust each other — that's what your SSH config means. v1.9 lets your agents use it. List your machines in one static `nodes.json`, and every broker dials every peer over plain `ssh <node> embassy peer-stdio`: no listener, no keys managed by Embassy, no discovery protocol, no second delivery system. Remote routes appear in your tables as `alias@host`, consent edges keep exactly one owning broker, and a cross-machine handoff is `delivered` precisely when the destination broker has durably accepted it — from that moment the destination's ledger owns provider delivery, and anything lost after authorization settles ambiguous, never replayed. The whole feature is one route kind, one transport, and three protocol methods riding the same v3 attempt machine every local message uses.

And the PM seat is now portable: `embassy register-peer` plus a blocking `embassy await` turns any shell-capable harness into a first-class peer — including harnesses that give every tool call a brand-new shell, because the token principal travels by stdin and lives in the agent's own context. Only the token's hash ever touches disk.

Verification: 567 tests and the full soak from cold worktrees; fake-SSH conformance across framing, correlation, catalog redaction, and every post-authorization fault; two adversarial rounds per pillar; and a live two-machine drill.

Upgrade: `npm install -g agent-embassy@1.9.0` on each machine, write your `nodes.json`, restart the brokers.
